families.tonal green, corner only: Today's room and ink kept, links green or a neutral stone; the only change is in the green's own strengths and halos, the section hues, or a faint wash in the greeting's corner. Looks like today.
families.warm companion, today's room: A warm second colour (honey amber, coral or rose) on the links, the greeting's corner and the top afterglow, over a room that is still today's green-black with cool-neutral words.
families.blue light, today's room: Sky, azure or dusk-blue light in the greeting's corner and the top afterglow, with cyan-to-blue links, over today's (or a slightly calmer) green-black room; the blue lives in light, not in the solids.
families.violet light, today's room: Lilac or violet light in the greeting's corner and afterglow, with lilac or periwinkle links, over today's green-black room (at most a lavender breath in the lines and words).
families.warm room, warm fittings: The whole room warmed: moss or olive-black cards, ivory or linen words, and a warm companion (brass, sand, a lamp-amber corner) for the links, so the mood changes all the way down the page.
families.warm room, cool links: The same moss-warm room with ivory or linen words, but its links and corner light are cool (sky, cobalt or orchid-violet): warmth in the solids, cool colour in the light.
families.blue room: Blue carried in the page's solids: navy selected fills and the family's chat bubbles, steel-blue hairlines and field borders, cool moonlit words, over a near-black ground; the page reads blue at a glance.
families.teal-tinted ground: The ground and cards themselves tinted a deep teal or petrol, so every page turns one blue-green colour family, with steel or cream words on it.
families.lifted grey ground: The black lifted a clear step to a grey-green slate, with warm soft words and no companion colour.
families.lantern haze, re-dyed sections: A warm lantern haze hanging over the top of every page, the sections re-dyed in festival colours (persimmon outings, teal seasons), jade links and cool moonlit words on a warm-grey room.
families.wood-panelled room: The cards themselves turned warm wood (walnut or crate-brown) edged in bronze or russet, with gilt or apricot headings and bronze or putty monitor cases over today's black: the page reads as furniture, whatever colour the links are.
families.sand trim on night slate: Cool night-slate cards (a faint blue-green) trimmed in warm pale sand: sand-gold headings, sand card edges and putty monitor cases, with turquoise links and little coloured light; a cool room with warm lettering.
families.wine-dark room: Plum, claret or rose carried in the solids (card fills, the family's bubbles, tiles and the monitors' cases) with orchid or rose lettering on the headings, over today's black; the page reads wine-dark at a glance.
families.slate console, pewter cases: Cool blue-grey slate cards and fields (plain, indigo-dyed or sea-fog), grey pewter, iron or lichen-clay monitor cases and edges, cream, linen or neutral words, over today's green-black; the exact phosphor is the one light and any companion (periwinkle, steel-blue, a madder dot) is a quiet accent, not a colour wash.
families.ruled composing room: A type-led page set like print: the panels opened into ruled sections (a rule over each heading instead of a boxed card), a phosphor cursor after every page title and mono bylines, in slate-console colours (black paper, newsprint words, pewter rules, blue-pencil marks); the setting, not the colour, is the idea.
families.indigo cloth, green glass: Two materials: the family's things (the bar, the cards, their bubbles and chips) in a violet-indigo cloth, the machine's on green-black glass, with cream words and spaced mono capitals over the sections; the page reads indigo-and-green at a glance, not navy.
families.zinc trays, lichen marks: Galvanised zinc-grey cards a clear step lighter than the ground, each panel headed by its own darker strip like a tray, cool white words, lichen-green small capitals and leaf marks, an underline for the page you are on; the machine's screens stay dark glass.
families.moss formica, blue-black ink: A kitchen's moss-green formica cards with olive legends and edges, typewritten headings, and blue-black ink in the fields and the family's bubbles, over today's black: the cool colour is in the solids the family writes in, not in the light.
families.black glass in a grey console: Depth turned inward: the ground lifted to a green-grey console and the cards sunk darker than it, black glass set into the panel, with scope-green labels and blue-black logbook ink for what the family writes and presses.
families.warm stoneware room: Cards and fields in warm umber, almond or oxblood-brown stoneware (not wood grain, not wine), ecru or washi words, iron monitor cases and a lacquer-red or linen accent, over today's green-black with the phosphor the one light.
families.silk-screened front panel: The page as an instrument's front panel: sections silk-screened on black metal with legends set into their rules, graphite modules, blue-grey keys and small lamps; the panel hardware, not a colour wash, is the idea.
families.frosted pewter, glacier links: Frosted pewter panes for the family's things with timber bands above and below, cork-brown dates, glacier-blue links and snow-white condensed words over today's green-black; a cold lodge, not a blue room.
families.dusk-violet paper on moss: The family's things on muted violet-dusk paper (heather clay, iris dusk) over green-black moss, pale paper-white words, graphite wells and little other colour: a soft purple-grey room, not wine.
families.flight-strip bays: Every row a slate strip racked in its own bay with black between, scopes set flush into the console; the rack-and-bay structure, not the colour, is the idea.
families.sage greenbar ledger: Cards and rows banded in muted sage-leaf green-grey like green-bar paper, apple-cream words and misty blue-grey accents over today's green-black: a soft green-grey room, not formica, not teal.
families.mimic-line track: Structure as the idea: every sequence hung from one pewter-blue track line with lamp stops and a timetable margin of times, slate plates on it; the control-room mimic line, not a colour wash.
families.bakelite wireless set: A thirties radio set: Bakelite claret-brown case plates, porcelain-white type, old-rose labels and a tuning-scale rule, with the green of its magic-eye tube the only light; the set, not a wine wash, is the idea.
families.felt rock pool: Soft cut felt at night: sea-slate felt for the family's things, coral and shell felt for their marks and dates, a soft serif to read, black water between, the phosphor as the pool's one light.
families.arcade after hours: An arcade after closing: oat-coloured tiles racked like cabinets, printed ruled forms, pixel sprites on every mark and VT323 labels, with only the screens running in bright green.
families.text-mode windows: The page drawn as green-screen software: flat steel windows with names set into their frames, double-framed dialogs to act in, unboxed rows, a fading highlight bar and reverse video for where you are.
families.programme listing: Structure as the idea: every part a band with its heading in a column inside it, every list one-line rows read across dotted leaders to a column of facts, like a printed TV or radio listing on slate.
families.glass cockpit: A night cockpit: the family's things on matte instrument plates grouped by fine demarcation lines with legends in the breaks, the machine on flush display units in screwed faceplates, each colour holding one fixed meaning.
families.porcelain star atlas: A star atlas set as a book: one centred serif column on a green-black dome, porcelain words and cobalt hairlines, each part of the site a disc in its own star colour.
families.bakelite text-mode windows: Text-mode windows, double-framed dialogs and reverse-video selection cut from claret-oxblood Bakelite with porcelain type; the software grammar in the wireless set's materials.
families.braun faceplate: Quiet warm-grey hardware in the manner of a Braun appliance: every page a faceplate, measures as dials, one green key, phosphor only on the displays.
families.bench oscilloscope: A bench scope's instrument-grey panel with engraved one-size type, ivory legends and oxblood knobs, the phosphor only where the beam traces.
families.night station timetable: A station at night: the conversation on a concourse, every part a numbered line in enamel colour on petrol-dark, phosphor only on departure boards.
families.blueprint operator manual: An operator's manual: every part a numbered plate led by its own figure drawn in blueprint blue on green-black, phosphor only where live.
families.docked terminal column: Two zones side by side: one lit glass column for the machine docked beside a grounded slate desk mat with indigo keys for the family's things.
families.handheld timeline: A four-green pocket handheld: chunky pixel boxes and sprites, every page strung along one timeline with NOW lit on it.
families.night gallery: The page hung as an exhibition after hours: one size of type, a wall label for everything, the green screens as the lit exhibits.
families.violet flight console: A 1969 flight console: a violet flight-plan drawing leads every section, rows of lamps for status, phosphor only on what is live.
families.videotex service: A videotex terminal service: one thing at a time under a mosaic band, numbered contents, a row of keys along the foot of every screen.
families.long-persistence instrument: One lit phosphor instrument per page tracing the family's weeks in bloom and afterglow, over a printed graphite legend whose rows light its marks.
families.glow-ink zine: A photocopied zine lit up: cut-and-paste blocks, glowing ink and hand-set headings, the page as a self-published pamphlet rather than a machine.
families.ceefax evening: Broadcast teletext: blocky double-height headings, flat saturated teletext colours on black and numbered pages, one screen of text at a time.
families.zenith desk: A mid-century console set into a desk: a warm cabinet with the machine's screen set in it, the family's things laid on the desk surface around it.
families.single quote: One large quotation or line per page, set big and alone, everything else pushed quiet beneath it: the page as a single statement.
